A2780 staged model comparison

Mechanistic equations, Delta-BIC rankings, and explicitly labeled fitted graph grids for the four-stage analysis.

Each teaching table shows the five leading candidates plus the simplest tested candidate when it is not already present. Absolute BIC values and complete parameter vectors are retained in the appendix and outputs/csv.

Stage 1

Untreated monoculture

Top five model and pooling combinations per cell line. Both seeding densities are fitted jointly with fixed day-zero populations.

Stage 1 notation key

\(X_i(t)\)
Observed total population for cell line \(i\); \(i=N\) means A2780Naive and \(i=C\) means A2780cis.
\(\dot X_i=dX_i/dt\)
Rate of change of that total population, in measured cells per day.
\(G_i(X_i,t)\)
Candidate intrinsic growth law: logistic, theta-logistic, Gompertz, hard-lag theta-logistic, Baranyi-adjusted theta-logistic, or smooth-adaptation theta-logistic.
\(r_i,K_i,\theta_i\)
Intrinsic growth rate, carrying capacity, and optional theta-logistic shape.
\(\tau_i,q_{0,i},\lambda_{A,i}\)
Optional hard-lag duration, Baranyi initial physiological-state parameter, or smooth adaptation rate. Only the parameter belonging to the candidate being fitted is used.

Stage 2

Treated monoculture

Top five whole-cell-line fits per cell line. Each model fits 20k and 30k across IC25, IC50, and IC75 while inheriting untreated growth.

Stage 2 notation key

\(X_i(t)\)
Total population in a one-state treatment model for cell line \(i\).
\(P_i(t),D_i(t)\)
Proliferating/live and damaged-but-still-visible compartments used only by the transit model.
\(S(t),T(t)\)
Drug-sensitive and drug-tolerant latent A2780cis subpopulations used only by the population-balance model; \(C=S+T\).
\(\widehat y_i(t)\)
Predicted observable: \(X_i\), \(P_i+\tfrac12D_i\), or \(S+T\), depending on the candidate.
\(G_i\)
The exact growth family and effective density-specific parameters inherited from Stage 1.
\(A_i(t)\)
Dimensionless time-activation term. It is 0 before onset and then turns drug action on either abruptly or gradually, depending on the timing candidate.
\(R(t;\lambda_i,t_{\mathrm{on},i})\)
Delayed ramp shorthand: \(\mathbf{1}_{t>t_{\mathrm{on},i}}[1-e^{-\lambda_i(t-t_{\mathrm{on},i})}]\).
\(H_i(z)\)
Hill dose-response term: \(H_i(z)=E_{\max,i}z^{h_i}/(EC_{50,i}^{h_i}+z^{h_i}+\varepsilon)\). It sets dose strength, not timing.
\(A_i(t)H_i(z)\)
The active per-capita treatment effect applied to a live/proliferating state. Transit models route this effect into a damaged-visible compartment before clearance.

Why the derivatives differ: \(dX/dt\), \(dP/dt\), and \(dS/dt\) are rates for different biological state variables, not interchangeable names for the same quantity.

Stage 2 timing audit

Onset and gradual-effect combinations

All five timing hypotheses use one joint objective over the same 12 treated-monoculture trajectories. The A2780Naive delayed Hill-ramp and A2780cis sensitive/tolerant population model are otherwise unchanged. Boundary flags and multistart results remain in outputs/csv/monoculture_treated.

Timing-audit notation key

\(R(t;\lambda_i,t_{\mathrm{on},i})\)
Delayed gradual activation: \(R(t;\lambda_i,t_{\mathrm{on},i})=\mathbf{1}_{t>t_{\mathrm{on},i}}\left[1-e^{-\lambda_i(t-t_{\mathrm{on},i})}\right]\). It equals 0 before onset and approaches 1 after onset.
\(\mathbf{1}_{t>t_{\mathrm{on},i}}\)
Pure onset switch. It is 0 before the fitted onset time and 1 after onset, with no gradual ramp.
\(\lambda_i\)
Activation speed in day\(^{-1}\). Larger \(\lambda_i\) means the delayed effect reaches full strength faster.
IDModelPoolingEquationdelta_BICRole

Stage 3

Untreated coculture

Top five coupled competition models across both densities and all three mix ratios. Lineage growth is inherited from untreated monoculture.

Stage 3 notation key

\(N(t),C(t)\)
A2780Naive and total A2780cis populations, respectively.
\(\dot N,\dot C\)
Lineage-specific rates of change. These are coupled because each lineage contributes to the other's crowding.
\(L_N=N+\alpha_{NC}C\)
Effective competitive load perceived by A2780Naive; \(L_N\) is a load, not another population compartment.
\(L_C=C+\alpha_{CN}N\)
Effective competitive load perceived by A2780cis.
\(G_N,G_C\)
Stage-1 lineage growth laws evaluated under the coculture competitive loads.
\(d_N,d_C\)
Optional first-order lineage loss rates in the competition-plus-death candidate.

Stage 4

Treated coculture

Top five linked treatment hypotheses across all treated monoculture and coculture environments. Coculture treatment is IC50 at 1.0 uM (Hill effect signal z = 0.50). Stage-2 drug parameters are inherited within a +/-5% validation margin; every additional context effect is named explicitly. Stage 2 nominally selected joint_ic_effect_transit_death, but Stage 4 uses the best population-balance-compatible joint_ic_effect_two_population candidate (Delta BIC=1.22); the mechanisms are not separated by Delta BIC >= 2.

Stage 4 notation key

\(N(t),C(t)\)
Total A2780Naive and A2780cis populations. For the resistant population-balance model, \(C=S+T\).
\(X_i(t)\)
Compact lineage placeholder used in the BIC table: \(X_i=N\) for \(i=N\), and \(X_i=C\) for \(i=C\).
\(M_N,M_C\)
Dimensionless coculture modifiers multiplying the inherited Stage-2 drug effects.
\(A_N(t),A_C(t)\)
Cell-line-specific treatment timing rules selected in Stage 2. A2780Naive uses delayed ramp activation; A2780cis uses the BIC-selected timing rule from the Stage 2 audit.
\(H_N(z),H_{CS}(z),H_{CT}(z)\)
Inherited Stage-2 Hill dose-response terms for Naive, cis sensitive-like, and cis tolerant-like treatment effects. Their products with \(A_i(t)\) are the actual time- and dose-dependent kill/damage rates.
\(f_{T0}^{\mathrm{co}},H_{CT}^{\mathrm{co}}\)
Coculture-adjusted initial tolerant fraction and tolerant-state Hill kill term.
\(\rho_T\)
Multiplier on tolerant-state growth in treated coculture; \(\rho_T=1\) means no growth-context change.

Stage 4 expanded treated-coculture equations

The BIC table below names the candidate-specific change. The full linked system inherits Stage 1 growth, Stage 2 treatment timing/Hill response, and Stage 3 coculture competition/death.

\[C=S+T,\qquad L_N=N+\alpha_{NC,d}C,\qquad L_C=C+\alpha_{CN,d}N\]
\[G_N^{\mathrm{co}}=G_N(N,L_N,t)-d_NN,\qquad G_C^{\mathrm{co}}=G_C(C,L_C,t)-d_CC\]
\[M_N=e^{\beta_NL_N/K_{N,d}},\qquad M_C=e^{\beta_CL_C/K_C}\]
\[f_{T0}^{\mathrm{co}}=\operatorname{logit}^{-1}\!\left(\operatorname{logit}(f_{T0})+\delta_f\right),\qquad H_{CT}^{\mathrm{co}}(z)=e^{\gamma_T}H_{CT}(z),\qquad \rho_T=e^{\gamma_{r,T}}\]
\[\frac{dN}{dt}=G_N^{\mathrm{co}}-M_NA_N(t)H_N(z)N\]
\[\frac{dS}{dt}=G_C^{\mathrm{co}}\frac{S}{C}-M_CA_C(t)H_{CS}(z)S\]
\[\frac{dT}{dt}=\rho_TG_C^{\mathrm{co}}\frac{T}{C}-M_CA_C(t)H_{CT}^{\mathrm{co}}(z)T\]

How to read the candidate rows: strict inheritance sets the extra coculture modifiers to their neutral values; load-scaled candidates estimate one or more \(\beta\) terms; tolerant-state candidates also estimate \(\delta_f\), \(\gamma_T\), and/or \(\gamma_{r,T}\).

Summary

Equation progression

The selected models build sequentially. Every growth, density, dose, delay, population-balance, competition, death, context-scaling, initial-condition, observation, and model-selection term used by the winning pipeline is defined below.

Design, density pooling, and initial conditions

\[s_d=\begin{cases}-1,&d=20\mathrm{k}\\+1,&d=30\mathrm{k}\end{cases}\]
\[p_d=p_{\mathrm{center}}e^{s_d\delta_p},\qquad |\delta_p|\le \ln(1.05)\]
\[U_d=\begin{cases}67,&d=20\mathrm{k}\\100,&d=30\mathrm{k}\end{cases}\]
\[X_i(0)=U_d\qquad\text{(monoculture cell line }i\text{)}\]
\[N(0)=f_{\mathrm{mix}}U_d,\qquad C(0)=(1-f_{\mathrm{mix}})U_d\qquad\text{(coculture)}\]
\[S(0)=(1-f_{T0})C(0),\qquad T(0)=f_{T0}C(0)\]
\[y_N(t)=N(t),\qquad y_C(t)=C(t)=S(t)+T(t)\]
\[[x]_+=\max(x,0)\]

The density contrast is symmetric and bounded at plus-or-minus five percent. Untreated partial pooling applies it to r and K; treated partial pooling applies it to treatment amplitudes; untreated coculture partial pooling applies it to both competition coefficients together. Starting populations are fixed and are never kinetic parameters.

1. Intrinsic untreated monoculture growth

A2780Naive: Baranyi-adjusted theta-logistic growth.

\(\displaystyle \frac{dX}{dt}=\alpha_B(t)rX\left[1-\left(\frac{X}{K}\right)^{\theta}\right],\quad \alpha_B(t)=\frac{q_0}{q_0+e^{-rt}}\)

A2780cis: Smooth adaptation theta-logistic growth.

\(\displaystyle \frac{dX}{dt}=A(t)rX\left[1-\left(\frac{X}{K}\right)^{\theta}\right],\quad A(t)=1-e^{-\lambda_A t}\)

The displayed equations are read from the selected Stage 1 baseline artifact when this report is built. The exact winning family, including any fitted lag or adaptation term, and its density-specific effective parameters are inherited by all later stages. The Baranyi candidate is used only as a phenomenological lag description here; its original biological interpretation was developed for microbial growth and is not evidence of an ovarian-cancer mechanism.

2. Add treated-monoculture effects

\[z=\begin{cases}0.25,&D=0.67\,\mu\mathrm{M}\;(\mathrm{IC}_{25})\\0.50,&D=1.00\,\mu\mathrm{M}\;(\mathrm{IC}_{50})\\0.75,&D=1.47\,\mu\mathrm{M}\;(\mathrm{IC}_{75})\end{cases}\]
\[A_N(t)=\mathbf{1}_{t>t_{\mathrm{on},N}}\left[1-e^{-\lambda_N(t-t_{\mathrm{on},N})}\right]\]
\[A_C(t)=\mathbf{1}_{t>t_{\mathrm{on},C}}\]
\[\varepsilon=10^{-12}\]
\[H_{N,d}(z)=\frac{E_{\max,N,d}z^{h_N}}{EC_{50,N}^{h_N}+z^{h_N}+\varepsilon}\]
\[H_{CS,d}(z)=\frac{E_{\max,CS,d}z^4}{0.5^4+z^4+\varepsilon},\qquad H_{CT,d}(z)=\frac{E_{\max,CT,d}z^4}{0.5^4+z^4+\varepsilon}\]
\[E_{\max,i,d}=E_{\max,i,\mathrm{center}}e^{s_d\delta_{E,i}},\qquad |\delta_{E,i}|\le\ln(1.05)\]
\[\frac{dN}{dt}=G_N(N,t)-A_N(t)H_{N,d}(z)N\]
\[C=S+T\]
\[\frac{dS}{dt}=G_C(C,t)\frac{S}{C}-A_C(t)H_{CS,d}(z)S\]
\[\frac{dT}{dt}=G_C(C,t)\frac{T}{C}-A_C(t)H_{CT,d}(z)T\]

The A2780Naive winner is delayed Hill-ramp kill. The A2780cis winner has separate sensitive and tolerant kill amplitudes and an estimated initial tolerant fraction. A five-model timing audit selected cis_onset_only by BIC; onset, gradual activation, shared-onset, and bounded-onset alternatives remain in the ranking rather than being silently discarded.

3. Add untreated-coculture competition and death

\[C=S+T\]
\[\alpha_{NC,d}=\alpha_{NC,\mathrm{center}}e^{s_d\delta_\alpha},\qquad \alpha_{CN,d}=\alpha_{CN,\mathrm{center}}e^{s_d\delta_\alpha}\]
\[L_N=N+\alpha_{NC,d}C,\qquad L_C=C+\alpha_{CN,d}N\]
\[G_N^{\mathrm{co}}=G_N(N,L_N,t)-d_NN\]
\[G_C^{\mathrm{co}}=G_C(C,L_C,t)-d_CC\]
\[\frac{dN}{dt}=G_N^{\mathrm{co}},\qquad \frac{dC}{dt}=G_C^{\mathrm{co}}\qquad\text{(untreated coculture)}\]

The winner is asymmetric competition with lineage-specific death. The two competition coefficients may differ by direction; their common density contrast is bounded at plus-or-minus five percent. Death rates are shared across density. Every selected monoculture growth parameter, including a lag/adaptation parameter when present, remains fixed.

4. Fully expanded treated-coculture winner

\[D=1.0\,\mu\mathrm{M}=\mathrm{IC}_{50},\qquad z=0.50\]
\[M_N=\exp\!\left(\operatorname{clamp}\!\left[\beta_N\frac{L_N}{K_{N,d}},-4,4\right]\right),\qquad M_C=\exp\!\left(\operatorname{clamp}\!\left[\beta_C\frac{L_C}{K_C},-4,4\right]\right)\]
\[f_{T0}^{\mathrm{co}}=\operatorname{logit}^{-1}\!\left[\operatorname{logit}(f_{T0})+\delta_f\right]\]
\[H_{CT,d}^{\mathrm{co}}(0.50)=e^{\gamma_T}H_{CT,d}(0.50),\qquad \rho_T=e^{\gamma_{r,T}}\]
\[\frac{dN}{dt}=G_N^{\mathrm{co}}-M_NA_N(t)H_{N,d}(0.50)N\]
\[\frac{dS}{dt}=G_C^{\mathrm{co}}\frac{S}{C}-M_CA_C(t)H_{CS,d}(0.50)S\]
\[\frac{dT}{dt}=\rho_TG_C^{\mathrm{co}}\frac{T}{C}-M_CA_C(t)H_{CT,d}^{\mathrm{co}}(0.50)T\]
\[C=S+T,\qquad L_N=N+\alpha_{NC,d}C,\qquad L_C=C+\alpha_{CN,d}N\]

This is the selected load_plus_tolerant_context model. Intrinsic growth and untreated competition/death parameters are fixed from Stages 1 and 3. Stage 2 drug parameters and the BIC-selected timing architecture are inherited within a plus-or-minus five-percent validation window. Its fitted context structure is total-load scaling, an initial tolerant-fraction shift, and tolerant-kill attenuation; modifiers not named by this winner are fixed at their neutral values.

Fitting, scale normalization, and BIC selection

\[s_j=\max_t y_j(t)\]
\[\mathrm{SSE}_{\mathrm{scaled}}=\sum_j\sum_t\left[\frac{y_j(t)-\widehat y_j(t)}{s_j}\right]^2\]
\[\mathrm{SSE}_{\mathrm{raw}}=\sum_j\sum_t\left[y_j(t)-\widehat y_j(t)\right]^2\]
\[\mathrm{BIC}=n\ln\!\left(\frac{\mathrm{SSE}_{\mathrm{scaled}}}{n}\right)+k\ln n\]

Small-to-large trajectory normalization. Each trajectory \(j\) is divided by its own observed peak \(s_j\). A 500-cell trajectory and a 4,000-cell trajectory therefore contribute comparable relative errors instead of the larger curve dominating merely because its residuals have larger units. The scaled SSE is dimensionless and drives optimization and BIC; raw SSE in squared cell-count units is also exported for scale-aware interpretation.

What is jointly fitted. Every candidate is fitted across all trajectories stated in its stage with one objective. In the canonical report, image tiles are averaged within wells and then biological samples are averaged at each time point. The sample-aware report preserves sample-level trajectories after within-well averaging and displays their between-sample uncertainty bands.

BIC counting. Here \(n\) is the total number of fitted time-point observations across all joint trajectories, not the number of wells, tiles, or environments. The count \(k\) includes every freely optimized center, shape, treatment, context, and pooling-contrast parameter. Fixed inherited parameters and fixed day-zero populations are not counted again. Lower BIC is better only relative to candidates fitted to the same observations and objective; it is not proof that the winning biological mechanism is true.

How to read Delta BIC. For candidate m, Delta BIC(m) = BIC(m) - minimum BIC, so the table winner is always zero. As descriptive evidence bands, 0-2 means little separation from the winner, 2-6 indicates positive separation, 6-10 strong separation, and values above 10 very strong separation. These are relative model-selection heuristics, not probabilities, confidence intervals, or proof of mechanism. Comparisons are valid only within a table whose candidates use the same observations and residual objective.

Initial conditions and time origin. Day zero is fixed at 67 measured cells for 20k seeding and 100 for 30k seeding. The first observed point is day 1. These anchors are passed through the package's fixed-initial-time and initial-state builder interface and are not estimated kinetic parameters.

Pooling. Shared models use one parameter value across 20k and 30k. Partial pooling permits only \(r\) and \(K\), or the stage-specific named effects, to differ through symmetric log contrasts bounded at plus-or-minus five percent: \(p_{20k}=p_c e^{-\delta_p}\), \(p_{30k}=p_c e^{\delta_p}\), \(|\delta_p|\le\ln(1.05)\). Fully independent density fits are retained as diagnostics but cannot silently become inherited defaults.

Fit validity. A fit is rejected if any parameter, prediction, SSE, or BIC is non-finite, or if its objective retains the failure sentinel. Boundary profiles expand requested bounds and accept an expansion only when the improvement is scientifically material under the configured BIC and margin rules. Multistart results and parameter-stability summaries are retained where that stage uses multistart optimization.

Uncertainty and weighting. Error ribbons show empirical variation; they are not inverse-variance weights in the canonical scaled-SSE objective. Later-stage fits inherit only eligible finite winners and record the exact source family and parameters in inheritance audit CSVs. This prevents a downstream stage from quietly replacing a selected lag, growth, dose-response, or competition law.

Symbol and function guide

This glossary states what every symbol does biologically and mathematically. A symbol with subscript d can differ between 20k and 30k only through the explicitly bounded density-pooling rule.

Populations and indices

\(t\)
Time in days from the fixed day-zero initial condition.
\(X_i(t)\)
Generic total population for a one-state monoculture model of cell line \(i\). This symbol avoids assigning a biological compartment that the model does not contain.
\(N(t)\)
A2780Naive population when both lineages are modeled explicitly.
\(P_i(t),D_i(t)\)
Proliferating/live and damaged-visible states used only in the transit-compartment model.
\(S(t),T(t)\)
Latent drug-sensitive and drug-tolerant A2780cis subpopulations used only in the population-balance model.
\(C(t)=S(t)+T(t)\)
Total observed A2780cis population. The experiment does not separately observe \(S\) and \(T\).
\(\widehat y_i(t)\)
Model prediction on the observed scale. It equals \(X_i\), \(P_i+\tfrac12D_i\), or \(S+T\), according to model structure.
\(\dot X=dX/dt\)
Derivative notation for a state's rate of change. Different letters mean distinct biological states, not inconsistent names for one quantity.
\(i\)
Lineage index: \(N\) for A2780Naive or \(C\) for A2780cis.
\(d\)
Starting-density environment: 20k or 30k.

Intrinsic growth

r_i
Intrinsic per-capita growth rate, with units day^-1.
K_i
Carrying capacity on the measured cell-count scale.
theta_i
Dimensionless theta-logistic shape. \(\theta=1\) recovers ordinary logistic growth; other values shift how sharply crowding suppresses growth.
tau_i
Hard-lag duration in days. The hard-lag candidate sets intrinsic growth to zero until \(t>\tau_i\), then switches the fitted theta-logistic law on.
q0_i
Positive Baranyi initial-state parameter. It defines \(\alpha_B(t)=q_0/(q_0+e^{-r_it})\), which smoothly raises the fraction of the intrinsic growth rate expressed over time.
lambda_A,i
Smooth adaptation rate in day\(^{-1}\). It defines \(A_i(t)=1-e^{-\lambda_{A,i}t}\), equivalent to \(dA_i/dt=\lambda_{A,i}(1-A_i)\) with \(A_i(0)=0\).
[x]_+
Positive part \([x]_+=\max(x,0)\), used in monoculture fits to prevent the inherited growth term from becoming artificial negative crowding death above K.

Starting density and mixture

U_d
Fixed total at day zero: 67 for 20k and 100 for 30k.
f_mix
Nominal A2780Naive fraction from the 25:75, 50:50, or 75:25 mixture label.
f_T0
Estimated initial tolerant fraction within the A2780cis population.
s_d
Density sign, -1 for 20k and +1 for 30k, used to create symmetric deviations around a cell-line center.
delta_p
Log-scale density contrast bounded by \(|\delta_p|\le\ln(1.05)\), so an eligible effective parameter can deviate by at most five percent in either direction.

Drug dose and Hill response

D
Physical drug concentration in uM.
z
Normalized IC effect level: 0.25, 0.50, or 0.75 for IC25, IC50, or IC75.
Emax_i
Maximum per-capita drug-effect amplitude, with units day^-1.
EC50_i
Effect level or concentration at which the Hill term reaches half of Emax.
h_i
Dimensionless Hill coefficient controlling dose-response steepness.
H_i(z)
Hill dose-response function. It converts dose/effect level into a potential per-capita kill or damage rate; it does not encode treatment delay.

Treatment activation A(t)

\[A_N(t)=\mathbf{1}_{t>t_{\mathrm{on},N}}\left[1-e^{-\lambda_N(t-t_{\mathrm{on},N})}\right]\]
\[A_C(t)=\mathbf{1}_{t>t_{\mathrm{on},C}}\]
A_i(t)
Dimensionless fraction of the eventual treatment effect active at time t. The Naive lineage uses a delayed ramp. The resistant lineage uses the BIC-selected cis_onset_only timing rule.
t_onset,i
Delay in days before drug action starts.
lambda_i
Activation rate in day^-1. Larger values switch treatment on faster. After onset, the activation half-time is \(\ln(2)/\lambda_i\).
\(k_i(t,z)=A_i(t)H_i(z)\)
Actual time- and dose-dependent per-capita treatment rate applied to the population.

Coculture interaction

alpha_NC
Effect of one cis cell on the crowding experienced by A2780Naive.
alpha_CN
Effect of one A2780Naive cell on the crowding experienced by A2780cis.
\(L_N=N+\alpha_{NC}C\)
Effective competitive load perceived by A2780Naive.
\(L_C=C+\alpha_{CN}N\)
Effective competitive load perceived by A2780cis.
d_N,d_C
Additional lineage-specific first-order loss rates in day^-1 in the competition-with-death model.

Coculture treatment modifier

beta_N,beta_C
Dimensionless coefficients linking normalized competitive load to drug-effect scaling.
M_i
Dimensionless multiplier on inherited drug action. \(M_i=1\) means no coculture modification, above one strengthens drug action, and below one weakens it.
delta_f
Log-odds shift in the latent tolerant fraction specifically in treated coculture: \(f_{T0}^{\mathrm{co}}=\operatorname{logit}^{-1}[\operatorname{logit}(f_{T0})+\delta_f]\).
gamma_T
Log multiplier on tolerant-compartment drug kill in coculture. Its exponential directly scales H_CT.
rho_T
Positive multiplier on tolerant-compartment growth in treated coculture. It equals exp(gamma_r,T); the selected estimate is approximately 1.25.
clamp(x,-4,4)
Numerical/biological guard limiting the log multiplier before exponentiation.
Current sign
The fitted beta_N and beta_C are negative, so larger competitive load attenuates effective drug action in the selected model.

Fit and selection quantities

y_j(t)
Observed value for trajectory j.
yhat_j(t)
ODE prediction for the same observation.
scale_j
Peak observed value of trajectory j, used so high-count trajectories do not dominate optimization.
n
Total observations in the joint objective.
k
Number of parameters estimated in that candidate, including pooling contrasts and context modifiers.
BIC
Bayesian information criterion; lower is preferred because it rewards fit while penalizing additional fitted parameters.

How every candidate model works

Stage 1: untreated monoculture candidates

Logistic

\[\frac{dX}{dt}=rX\left[1-\frac{X}{K}\right]_+\]

Growth is nearly exponential at low population and slows linearly with occupancy \(X/K\). It has the fewest mechanistic parameters.

Theta-logistic

\[\frac{dX}{dt}=rX\left[1-\left(\frac{X}{K}\right)^\theta\right]_+\]

Adds a shape parameter. This can move most growth suppression closer to or farther from carrying capacity without changing the low-density growth rate.

Gompertz

\[\frac{dX}{dt}=rX\ln\!\left(\frac{K}{X}\right)\]

Per-capita growth decreases logarithmically with population, producing asymmetric sigmoidal trajectories.

Simple-death diagnostic

\[\frac{dX}{dt}=rX\left[1-\frac{X}{K}\right]_+-dX\]

Tests whether an untreated first-order loss term is needed. It is diagnostic and is inherited only with strong identifiable BIC support.

Allee diagnostic

\[\frac{dX}{dt}=rX\left[1-\frac{X}{K}\right]_+\left(\frac{X}{A_{\mathrm{Allee}}}-1\right)\]

Tests for suppressed or negative growth below a critical population threshold. It is not treated as a default baseline.

Pooling: shared and partial-pooling versions use the same biological ODE. Partial pooling adds bounded density contrasts to r and K; independent fits are diagnostic only.

Stage 2: treated monoculture candidates

Anchored linear kill

\[\frac{dX}{dt}=G(X)-k_{\mathrm{kill}}DX\]

Immediate kill proportional to physical concentration. It is simple but cannot create a delayed rise-then-decline trajectory.

Anchored concentration-Hill kill

\[\frac{dX}{dt}=G(X)-\frac{E_{\max}D^h}{EC_{50}^h+D^h}X\]

Immediate saturating concentration response. It remains monotonic in time at fixed dose.

Time-decay kill

\[\frac{dX}{dt}=G(X)-k_{\mathrm{kill}}De^{-\lambda t}X\]

Drug action is strongest initially and wanes over time, representing clearance, adaptation, or loss of exposure and allowing later regrowth.

Immediate IC-Hill

\[\frac{dX}{dt}=G(X)-H(z)X\]

Uses normalized IC effect levels rather than physical concentration, with no onset delay.

Hill ramp

\[\frac{dX}{dt}=G(X)-\left(1-e^{-\lambda t}\right)H(z)X\]

Drug action accumulates from day zero.

Delayed Hill ramp

\[\frac{dX}{dt}=G(X)-A(t)H(z)X\]

Adds an explicit onset time before the accumulating effect. This is the selected A2780Naive mechanism.

Transit damage

\[\frac{dP}{dt}=G(P)-A(t)H(z)P,\qquad \frac{dD}{dt}=A(t)H(z)P-k_{\mathrm{clear}}D\]
\[\widehat y=P+\frac12D\]

Cells leave the proliferating live compartment, remain partly visible while damaged, and are cleared later. The candidate fixes Hill EC50=0.5 and h=4.

Sensitive/tolerant populations

\[\frac{dS}{dt}=G(S+T)\frac{S}{S+T}-A_C(t)H_{CS}(z)S,\qquad \frac{dT}{dt}=G(S+T)\frac{T}{S+T}-A_C(t)H_{CT}(z)T\]
\[\widehat y=S+T\]

Both latent states share one inherited total-growth law but have different kill amplitudes. Their initial split is controlled by f_T0. This is the selected A2780cis mechanism.

Intracellular platinum PK/PD

\[\frac{dc_i}{dt}=D-k_{\mathrm{efflux}}c_i,\qquad \frac{dc_k}{dt}=c_i-k_{\mathrm{repair}}c_k,\qquad \frac{dX}{dt}=G(X)-H(c_k)X\]

This literature-grounded diagnostic candidate adds lumped intracellular platinum and DNA-bound platinum states. Uptake and binding scales are fixed because cell-count-only trajectories cannot separately identify them from kill amplitude; intracellular platinum or DNA-adduct measurements would be needed for a fully mechanistic fit.

Timing audit: independent onset plus ramp; shared onset plus ramp; onset differences bounded within 0.5 day; resistant gradual-only; and resistant onset-only.

These timing candidates refit the same 12-trajectory objective through GrowthParameterEstimation.run_joint_multistart. BIC therefore compares the timing architectures with their different parameter counts on an identical data set.

Stage 3: untreated coculture candidates

Symmetric competition

\[\alpha_{NC}=\alpha_{CN}=\alpha,\qquad \frac{dN}{dt}=G_N(N+\alpha C),\qquad \frac{dC}{dt}=G_C(C+\alpha N)\]

Both lineages exert the same cross-crowding strength.

Asymmetric competition

\[\alpha_{NC}\ne\alpha_{CN},\qquad \frac{dN}{dt}=G_N(N+\alpha_{NC}C),\qquad \frac{dC}{dt}=G_C(C+\alpha_{CN}N)\]

Each lineage can affect the other differently.

Asymmetric competition plus death

\[\frac{dN}{dt}=G_N(L_N)-d_NN,\qquad \frac{dC}{dt}=G_C(L_C)-d_CC\]

Adds lineage-specific loss beyond competitive growth suppression. This is the selected Stage 3 model. All six density/mix environments are fitted together.

Strobl density-dependent-birth family

\[\frac{dS}{dt}=r_S\left(1-\frac{S+R}{K_S}\right)\left(1-\frac{2d_DD(t)}{D_{\max}}\right)S-d_SS,\qquad \frac{dR}{dt}=r_R\left(1-\frac{S+R}{K_R}\right)R-d_RR\]

The four main-paper reductions test neither cost nor turnover, growth cost only, turnover only, and growth cost plus turnover. The supplementary variants place the same relative cost in resistant carrying capacity, \(K_R=(1-c)K\), or resistant death, \(d_R=(1+c)d_T\). For untreated Stage 3, \(D(t)=0\).

Strobl density-dependent-death alternative

\[\frac{dS}{dt}=r_S\left(1-\frac{2d_DD(t)}{D_{\max}}\right)S-d_T^{\dagger}\frac{S+R}{K}S,\qquad \frac{dR}{dt}=r_RR-d_T^{\dagger}\frac{S+R}{K}R\]

This supplementary model moves density regulation from proliferation to death. It is fitted as a diagnostic because the paper's \(S/R\) phenotypes are mapped here to two separately measured A2780 cell lines. The mapping is useful as a structural benchmark but is not proof that the lines are interchangeable with within-tumor sensitive and resistant phenotypes.

Primary sources: Strobl et al. main paper, mathematical supplement, and authors' fitting code. The report preserves the published equation structures; A2780-specific parameter estimates are refitted against this experiment.

Stage 4: linked treated-coculture hypotheses

Strict inheritance

\[M_N=M_C=1\]

The same intrinsic drug vector acts in monoculture and coculture with no context modification.

Competitor-scaled

\[M_N=e^{\beta_N\alpha_{NC}C/K_N},\qquad M_C=e^{\beta_C\alpha_{CN}N/K_C}\]

Only the opposing lineage's contribution modifies drug action.

Load-scaled

\[M_N=e^{\beta_NL_N/K_N},\qquad M_C=e^{\beta_CL_C/K_C}\]

Total effective load, including self and competitor, modifies drug action. This is the BIC winner.

Load plus context amplitude

\[M_i=e^{\beta_iL_i/K_i+\gamma_i}\]

Adds a density-independent coculture shift gamma_i on top of load scaling.

Tolerant context shift

\[f_{T0}^{\mathrm{co}}=\operatorname{logit}^{-1}[\operatorname{logit}(f_{T0})+\delta_f],\qquad H_{CT}^{\mathrm{co}}=e^{\gamma_T}H_{CT}\]

Allows coculture to enrich the latent tolerant state and attenuate its kill rate while preserving the stage-2 sensitive/tolerant model.

Subpopulation load scaling

\[M_{CS}=e^{\beta_{CS}L_C/K_C},\qquad M_{CT}=e^{\beta_{CT}L_C/K_C}\]

Tests whether competitive load scales sensitive and tolerant kill differently without changing their initial composition.

Load plus tolerant context

\[M_N,M_C,\delta_f,\gamma_T\quad\text{jointly define load scaling and tolerant-state modification}\]

Combines total-load drug scaling with the resistant-state shift.

Load plus tolerant growth context

\[M_C=e^{\beta_C\,L_C/K_C},\qquad \left.\frac{dT}{dt}\right|_{\mathrm{growth}}=\rho_TG_C^{\mathrm{co}}\frac{T}{C},\qquad \rho_T=e^{\gamma_{r,T}}\]

Adds one bounded phenotype-specific growth-plasticity multiplier to the preceding model. This is the selected Stage 4 mechanism; BIC pays for the additional fitted parameter.

Fully free context diagnostic

\[\mathbf q_{\mathrm{drug}}^{\mathrm{co}}\ne\mathbf q_{\mathrm{drug}}^{\mathrm{mono}}\]

Fits separate complete drug vectors by context. It tests whether inheritance fails, but is deliberately diagnostic because it gives up mechanistic sharing.

Strobl linked-treatment benchmarks

\[\bar D(t)=\frac{D(t)}{D_{\max}},\qquad \text{drug modifies sensitive-cell proliferation by }1-2d_D\bar D(t)\]

Each Strobl variant is also fitted to the identical 24-trajectory Stage 4 objective. Physical cisplatin concentrations are normalized by the largest measured dose, 1.47 uM; \(d_D\) is refitted for A2780 rather than copied from the prostate-cancer parameterization. A2780cis receives no direct drug term because the paper defines \(R\) as fully resistant. This is a stringent, low-parameter benchmark and may fit poorly if A2780cis retains measurable cisplatin response.

Important: Stage 4 does not attach an arbitrary coefficient to every term. Growth and untreated interaction parameters are fixed from earlier stages, and the Stage 2 drug vector is restricted to a plus-or-minus five-percent inheritance window. Candidate-specific context terms are counted in BIC, and the fully free context vector remains diagnostic only.

How the four-stage handoff works

  1. Stage 1 learns intrinsic growth. Each cell line is fitted jointly across 20k and 30k. Its winning family and effective r/K/theta values become the biological growth baseline.
  2. Stage 2 learns treatment response. The Stage 1 growth law is fixed while all three monoculture doses and both densities determine delayed, Hill, transit, or population-balance parameters. A second joint BIC audit chooses whether resistant treatment needs onset, gradual activation, both, or timing shared with Naive.
  3. Stage 3 learns untreated interaction. Stage 1 growth remains fixed while both densities and all mixture ratios determine competition and death parameters.
  4. Stage 4 combines the mechanisms. Stage 1 growth and Stage 3 interaction are fixed. Stage 2 drug parameters are inherited within plus-or-minus five percent. BIC then tests strict inheritance, load effects, resistant-state shifts, tolerant growth plasticity, and a fully separate diagnostic vector across the combined treated data.
Selection

Selected inheritance path

The ledger records the exact fitted rows selected above. The running value is the sum of the displayed stage-local Delta BIC penalties. It is a comparison aid, not a new global BIC, because Stage 4 reuses treated-monoculture observations and only the data-selected path has been refitted end to end.

Preview

Conditional-refit provenance 

  

  

    How preview and refitting work
    
Preview switches among stored top-candidate trajectories immediately. Refit downstream sends the exact model and pooling path to a local Julia service, which calls the package fitting functions, carries fitted parameters into later stages, and caches the result by path.

    
If a selected treatment model lacks the latent states required by the linked Stage 4 equation, or a selected competition family cannot be inherited by that equation, Stages 1-3 are still recomputed and the result is labeled Partially refitted. The static GitHub Pages copy remains fully usable for preview but cannot start Julia by itself.

  






  
Notation
What pooling means

  
Pooling describes which experimental groups share a fitted parameter. It does not mean averaging cell lines together, and it is separate from averaging technical wells within a biological sample.

  

    
Shared pooling

    
One parameter value is fitted jointly to every included density or environment. For example, (r_{20k}=r_{30k}=r). All trajectories inform the same estimate, reducing free parameters but assuming no density-specific difference.

    
Partial pooling, partial_5pct

    
A shared center is fitted with a small, symmetric density contrast: (p_{20k}=p_{mathrm{center}}e^{-delta_p}), (p_{30k}=p_{mathrm{center}}e^{+delta_p}), and (|delta_p|leqln(1.05)). The densities may differ by roughly five percent in either direction while remaining anchored to one biological estimate. Which parameters receive this contrast is stated in each stage.

    
Independent diagnostic

    
Each density or group receives its own unconstrained parameter vector. This can reveal heterogeneity or model misspecification, but it uses more free parameters and is not automatically eligible for inheritance because the later stages require a coherent shared baseline.

    
Linked global

    
One combined objective is fitted across all linked monoculture and coculture trajectories. Intrinsic drug parameters are shared across contexts, while only the candidate's explicitly named coculture modifiers are added.

    
Strobl joint

    
The complete two-population Strobl equation is fitted jointly across the relevant density and mixture environments. Its parameter sharing follows that published model structure rather than the project's ordinary density-contrast rule.

    
Well and sample aggregation

    
Technical wells are first summarized within their experimental sample. A sample-aware analysis then retains between-sample variation and uncertainty. This observation-level aggregation changes the data entering the objective; it is distinct from parameter pooling.

  

  
BIC accounting: (k) counts parameters estimated in that candidate's objective. Parameters fixed from an earlier stage are inherited parameters, not free parameters again in the downstream BIC. A partial-pooling contrast is free and is counted once.
